title: One Country, Two Presidents: The Crisis in Venezuela

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日简报《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过 nytimes.com 免费直播部分采访，供所有人观看。

If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: A remarkable battle for power is playing out in Venezuela, with dueling claims to the president and talk of a coup.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉正在上演一场非凡的权力之争，出现了两位总统竞选者，甚至还有政变的传闻。

sentences.en: Nick Casey on the crisis in Caracas.
sentences.zh: 尼克·凯西报道加拉加斯的危机。

sentences.en: It's Friday, January 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月25日，星期五。

sentences.en: So on January 10th in Caracas, Venezuela, Nicolas Maduro put his hand on a book and swore himself in as president for another six-year term.
sentences.zh: 1月10日，在委内瑞拉加拉加斯，尼古拉斯·马杜罗手按宪法宣誓就职，开启了又一个六年任期。

sentences.en: Y haré cumplir todos los postulados y mandatos de la Constitución de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela
sentences.zh: 我将履行委内瑞拉玻利瓦尔共和国宪法的所有原则和授权，

sentences.en: para procurar defender la independencia y la integridad absoluta de la patria.
sentences.zh: 以捍卫祖国的独立和绝对完整。

sentences.en: Then two weeks later, in another part of Caracas, on a sunny day, a little-known lawmaker named Juan Guaidó
sentences.zh: 两周后，在加拉加斯的另一个地方，在一个阳光明媚的日子里，一位鲜为人知的议员名叫胡安·瓜伊多，

sentences.en: stood before a group of people and held a kind of citizen's swearing-in ceremony where he said he was the president of Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 他站在一群人面前，举行了一种公民宣誓仪式，宣布自己是委内瑞拉总统。

sentences.en: And he was prepared to lead the country himself.
sentences.zh: 并准备好亲自领导这个国家。

sentences.en: So two men are declaring themselves the president of Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 所以现在有两个人宣布自己是委内瑞拉总统。

sentences.en: One country, two presidents.
sentences.zh: 一个国家，两位总统。

sentences.en: And Nick, how is that possible?
sentences.zh: 尼克，这怎么可能？

sentences.en: What has been going on in Venezuela that leads these two men at the exact same time to declare themselves the rightful leader of the country?
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉到底发生了什么，导致这两个人同时宣布自己是该国的合法领导人？

sentences.en: Well, you have to turn the clock back to last year, just before the summer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得把时间拨回到去年，就在夏天之前。

sentences.en: Official campaigning for Venezuela's presidential election has kicked off with huge rallies by the candidates.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉总统大选的官方竞选活动已经拉开帷幕，候选人们举行了大规模的集会。

sentences.en: When Maduro was running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 当时马杜罗正在竞选连任。

sentences.en: Now remember, he'd been president of this country during this massive disaster in Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 记住，在委内瑞拉这场巨大的灾难期间，他一直担任这个国家的总统。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the summer, the currency was collapsing.
sentences.zh: 夏初时，货币正在崩溃。

sentences.en: People were losing even more of their savings than they ever had.
sentences.zh: 人们损失的积蓄比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: Hospitals were completely out of supplies.
sentences.zh: 医院完全没有物资供应。

sentences.en: And they had been for years.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续多年了。

sentences.en: I was there during that time.
sentences.zh: 那段时间我正好在那里。

sentences.en: I got sick.
sentences.zh: 我病了。

sentences.en: I got dengue.
sentences.zh: 我得了登革热。

sentences.en: And they weren't able to do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 他们对此束手无策。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: This was the state of the country that has the world's largest proven reserves of oil.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个拥有世界最大已探明石油储量的国家的状态。

sentences.en: It was at an all-time low.
sentences.zh: 它处于历史最低点。

sentences.en: And Nicolas Maduro was asking them to give him another six years as the president.
sentences.zh: 而尼古拉斯·马杜罗却要求他们再给他六年总统任期。

sentences.en: And that would seem quite counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这看起来非常违背常理。

sentences.en: What was his standing at that moment?
sentences.zh: 他当时的支持率如何？

sentences.en: How many people blamed him for the situation?
sentences.zh: 有多少人把这种情况归咎于他？

sentences.en: Everybody blamed him.
sentences.zh: 每个人都怪他。

sentences.en: You would go around in the neighborhoods in Caracas, and they would point at how skinny they were and say this is the consequence of the Maduro diet.
sentences.zh: 你在加拉加斯的街区走一走，人们会指着自己消瘦的身材说，这就是“马杜罗节食法”的后果。

sentences.en: The Maduro diet, named after the current president, Nicolas Maduro.
sentences.zh: “马杜罗节食法”，以现任总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗命名。

sentences.en: That's what it's called there when people have lost a bunch of weight.
sentences.zh: 当人们体重骤减时，当地人就这么称呼它。

sentences.en: Well, over the past year, 74% of Venezuelans lost an average of 8.7 kilos in weight.
sentences.zh: 过去一年里，74%的委内瑞拉人平均体重减轻了8.7公斤。

sentences.en: He's even laughed about that.
sentences.zh: 他甚至对此嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: He says he thinks it's funny.
sentences.zh: 他说他觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: This is a man who's shown very little sympathy for this massive crisis that the country is going through.
sentences.zh: 这个人对国家正在经历的巨大危机表现出的同情心微乎其微。

sentences.en: So you would think, under normal circumstances, that it would be impossible that this person would be re-elected by the country that had been, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会认为，在正常情况下，这个人在他第一个总统任期内把国家搞得如此糟糕，

sentences.en: so brought down during his first term as president.
sentences.zh: 是不可能连任的。

sentences.en: So then, here comes the night of the election, and the results come in, and Maduro's won.
sentences.zh: 然而，选举之夜到了，结果出来了，马杜罗赢了。

sentences.en: Venezuela's president, Nicolas Maduro, has been declared winner of Sunday's election.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗被宣布为周日选举的获胜者。

sentences.en: We won again.
sentences.zh: 我们又赢了。

sentences.en: We were triumphant again.
sentences.zh: 我们再次取得了胜利。

sentences.en: We've overcome all obstacles.
sentences.zh: 我们克服了所有障碍。

sentences.en: We are the strength of history transformed into a popular victory, permanent popular victory.
sentences.zh: 我们是转化为人民胜利的历史力量，是永恒的人民胜利。

sentences.en: He's going to be president for another six years.
sentences.zh: 他还要再当六年总统。

sentences.en: And to many Venezuelans, they found that terribly shocking.
sentences.zh: 许多委内瑞拉人感到极其震惊。

sentences.en: Today, the world have the eyes here in Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 今天，全世界的目光都聚焦在委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: What Venezuelans have at stake today is their own survival as a democratic nation.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉人今天所面临的风险是他们作为一个民主国家能否生存下去。

sentences.en: Venezuela is a dictatorship.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉是一个独裁国家。

sentences.en: The world can no longer turn a blind eye to that reality.
sentences.zh: 世界不能再对这一现实视而不见。

sentences.en: The whole manner in which this election was conducted was under a big cloud, and immediately you see countries outside of Venezuela condemning what had happened,
sentences.zh: 这次选举的整个过程都笼罩在阴云之下，你立刻就能看到委内瑞拉以外的国家谴责所发生的一切，

sentences.en: saying that the election may have been rigged, that they're not going to recognize Nicolas Maduro.
sentences.zh: 称选举可能存在舞弊，他们不会承认尼古拉斯·马杜罗。

sentences.en: ...are denouncing his win as a sham.
sentences.zh: ……谴责他的胜选是一场骗局。

sentences.en: Panama, Costa Rica, Chile, and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 巴拿马、哥斯达黎加、智利和美国

sentences.en: mission to the U.N.
sentences.zh: 驻联合国代表团

sentences.en: said they won't recognize the results of the election.
sentences.zh: 表示他们不会承认选举结果。

sentences.en: President Trump signing a new executive order this afternoon following the results of that controversial Venezuelan election.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统今天下午在争议性的委内瑞拉选举结果出炉后签署了一项新的行政命令。

sentences.en: The executive order is designed to try and prevent the Venezuelan government from selling off its assets.
sentences.zh: 该行政命令旨在试图阻止委内瑞拉政府出售其资产。

sentences.en: And yet, if you're in Venezuela, it looks like you're going to have Maduro as your president for another six years.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你身在委内瑞拉，看起来马杜罗还要再当六年的总统。

sentences.en: They said that you were obliged to vote.
sentences.zh: 他们说你必须去投票。

sentences.en: They said that people were coerced.
sentences.zh: 他们说人们受到了胁迫。

sentences.en: It's a lack of respect.
sentences.zh: 这简直是缺乏尊重。

sentences.en: So months passed.
sentences.zh: 几个月过去了。

sentences.en: People are generally depressed about where things are going to go.
sentences.zh: 人们对未来的走向普遍感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And throughout this process, people are asking, well, wait a second, where's the opposition here?
sentences.zh: 在整个过程中，人们都在问，等等，反对派在哪里？

sentences.en: Why are they not protesting?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不抗议？

sentences.en: Why are they not trying to stand up to what's going on or offer any alternative?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不站出来反抗正在发生的事情，或者提出任何替代方案？

sentences.en: He cracked down on dissenting voices.
sentences.zh: 他严厉打击异见声音。

sentences.en: Prominent opposition leaders were arrested or put under house arreSt.
sentences.zh: 著名的反对派领导人被捕或被软禁。

sentences.en: There was getting to be very little of the opposition left.
sentences.zh: 反对派几乎所剩无几。

sentences.en: The regime was going through and picking off leader after leader, often issuing orders of arrest for them.
sentences.zh: 政权不断地清除一个又一个领导人，通常会向他们发出逮捕令。

sentences.en: And they'd disappear.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就消失了。

sentences.en: You'd find them in Colombia.
sentences.zh: 你会发现他们在哥伦比亚。

sentences.en: You'd find them in Chile.
sentences.zh: 你会发现他们在智利。

sentences.en: The opposition was getting thinner and thinner at this point, to the point that either you had an arrest warrant against you or you thought there might be one soon.
sentences.zh: 反对派此时变得越来越弱，以至于要么你身上背着逮捕令，要么你觉得很快就会有。

sentences.en: And you had just many, many people, both politicians and supporters of the opposition, leaving the country.
sentences.zh: 有很多人，包括政客和反对派支持者，都离开了这个国家。

sentences.en: Because after an election like that, kind of what hope did you have to try to challenge this guy?
sentences.zh: 因为在那样一场选举之后，你还有什么希望去挑战这个家伙呢？

sentences.en: Then what happened?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, Maduro continued on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，马杜罗继续执政。

sentences.en: And he had his re-inauguration, which was January the 10th.
sentences.zh: 他在1月10日举行了重新就职典礼。

sentences.en: I think he thought everything was going to go very smoothly.
sentences.zh: 我想他以为一切都会非常顺利。

sentences.en: He had a big ceremony.
sentences.zh: 他举行了盛大的仪式。

sentences.en: Many of the people in his government attended.
sentences.zh: 他政府中的许多人都出席了。

sentences.en: And he said, we're starting another six-year term.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们开启了另一个六年任期。

sentences.en: And it's then that the opposition starts to leap into action.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，反对派开始采取行动。

sentences.en: Although parliament is now largely toothless, its leader, Juan Guaido, has vowed to fight back.
sentences.zh: 尽管议会现在基本上名存实亡，但其领导人胡安·瓜伊多誓言要反击。

sentences.en: We reaffirm the illegitimacy of Nicolas Maduro.
sentences.zh: 我们重申尼古拉斯·马杜罗的非法性。

sentences.en: The opposition had a card up its sleeve, which was the Venezuelan constitution.
sentences.zh: 反对派手中有一张王牌，那就是委内瑞拉宪法。

sentences.en: There are articles that they can use if a president has seized power illegally.
sentences.zh: 如果总统非法夺取权力，他们可以使用宪法中的条款。

sentences.en: And they say that this inauguration that he's done for himself was a seizing of power because he didn't win that election back last year.
sentences.zh: 他们说他为自己举行的这次就职典礼是夺权行为，因为他去年并没有赢得那场选举。

sentences.en: In this case, this triggers a mechanism in Venezuela whereby the legislature gets to take control of the country and decide who's going to be running it,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这触发了委内瑞拉的一种机制，即立法机构可以接管国家并决定由谁来管理，

sentences.en: in which case it gets to be the president of the National Assembly, who was Juan Guaido, the 35-year-old young lawmaker who no one had ever heard of,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，它将由国民议会议长担任，也就是胡安·瓜伊多，那位没人听说过的35岁年轻议员，

sentences.en: one of the last remaining men standing.
sentences.zh: 最后仅存的几个人之一。

sentences.en: He did something that no one in the opposition had been willing to do, which was to take Maduro
sentences.zh: 他做了一件反对派中没有人愿意做的事，那就是挑战马杜罗，

sentences.en: on by saying that he was actually the president of Venezuela, which was an extremely audacious move.
sentences.zh: 声称他才是委内瑞拉的总统，这是一个极其大胆的举动。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's really hard to underestimate how much risk is involved in taking on Maduro this way.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式挑战马杜罗所涉及的风险，怎么估计都不为过。

sentences.en: So beyond invoking obscure rules from the Constitution, what is Guaido's plan for how to execute this and knock out Maduro?
sentences.zh: 那么，除了援引宪法中晦涩的条款外，瓜伊多对于如何执行这一计划并击败马杜罗有什么打算？

sentences.en: Well, I think you saw some of it the day that he inaugurated himself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想在他宣誓就职的那天，你已经看到了一些端倪。

sentences.en: And this was a really surprising day for everybody that was covering this.
sentences.zh: 对于所有报道此事的记者来说，那真是令人惊讶的一天。

sentences.en: Because he went out, he had this big ceremony, and just within minutes of him declaring himself the president of Venezuela, you had an announcement from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为他走出来，举行了盛大的仪式，就在他宣布自己是委内瑞拉总统的几分钟内，美国就发布了公告，

sentences.en: that they were going to recognize him.
sentences.zh: 称他们将承认他。

sentences.en: Hola.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I'm Mike Pence, the vice president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 我是美国副总统迈克·彭斯。

sentences.en: And on behalf of President Donald Trump and all the American people, let me express the unwavering support of the United States as you, the people of Venezuela, raise your voices
sentences.zh: 我谨代表唐纳德·特朗普总统和全体美国人民，表达美国对你们——委内瑞拉人民——发出自由呼声的坚定支持。

sentences.en: in a call for freedom.
sentences.zh: 呼吁自由。

sentences.en: Nicolas Maduro is a dictator with no legitimate claim to power.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉斯·马杜罗是一位独裁者，没有任何合法的权力主张。

sentences.en: He's never won the presidency in a free and fair election.
sentences.zh: 他从未在自由公正的选举中赢得总统职位。

sentences.en: And he's maintained his grip of power by imprisoning anyone who dares to oppose him.
sentences.zh: 他通过监禁任何敢于反对他的人来维持对权力的控制。

sentences.en: The United States joined...
sentences.zh: 美国加入了……

sentences.en: And then you had an announcement from Canada that they were going to recognize him.
sentences.zh: 然后加拿大也宣布他们将承认他。

sentences.en: So let me say on behalf of Canada that we recognize and express our full support for the intern presidency of Venezuela,
sentences.zh: 我谨代表加拿大宣布，我们承认并全力支持委内瑞拉临时总统，

sentences.en: assumed by the president of the National Assembly, Juan Guaido.
sentences.zh: 由国民议会议长胡安·瓜伊多担任。

sentences.en: And then it just became sort of like dominoes.
sentences.zh: 然后这就像多米诺骨牌一样。

sentences.en: You had Costa Rica and Paraguay and Argentina.
sentences.zh: 哥斯达黎加、巴拉圭和阿根廷也加入了。

sentences.en: The vice president of Peru, Mercedes Arauz.
sentences.zh: 秘鲁副总统梅赛德斯·阿劳斯。

sentences.en: Peru and Brazil.
sentences.zh: 秘鲁和巴西。

sentences.en: Brazil also.
sentences.zh: 巴西也加入了。

sentences.en: And now we're going to be here.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要在这里了。

sentences.en: Colombia.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚。

sentences.en: Colombia.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚。

sentences.en: Reconocen a Juan Guaido como presidente de Venezuela y acompaña este proceso de transición hacia la democracia para que el pueblo venezolano se libere de la dictadura.
sentences.zh: 承认胡安·瓜伊多为委内瑞拉总统，并支持这一向民主过渡的进程，以便委内瑞拉人民从独裁统治中解放出来。

sentences.en: All of these countries suddenly said, now we no longer recognize Maduro.
sentences.zh: 所有这些国家突然宣布，我们不再承认马杜罗。

sentences.en: It's Guaido who's the president of Venezuela now.
sentences.zh: 现在瓜伊多才是委内瑞拉总统。

sentences.en: So what you could see was there must have been another part of this plan here, which wasn't just to make this crazy statement that he was the president,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出，这个计划肯定还有另一部分，不仅仅是发表那句疯狂的声明说他是总统，

sentences.en: but also potentially a back channel in which they had a lot of other countries lined up to go along with this plan when he did it on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 而且可能还有一个幕后渠道，他们在周三采取行动时，已经让许多其他国家排好队支持这个计划。

sentences.en: I have to say that I'm struck that all these major democracies are backing Guaido, who is not democratically elected as the leader of Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，令我震惊的是，所有这些主要民主国家都在支持瓜伊多，他并不是作为委内瑞拉领导人通过民主选举产生的。

sentences.en: Why exactly are they doing that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I'm surprised too, frankly, covering this.
sentences.zh: 是的，坦率地说，我也很惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, he wasn't elected and people didn't really know who he was.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他不是选出来的，人们真的不知道他是谁。

sentences.en: I think people are still trying to look under the hood of who this man is.
sentences.zh: 我想人们还在试图深入了解这个人到底是谁。

sentences.en: So what does it show?
sentences.zh: 那这说明了什么？

sentences.en: It shows that the international community has gotten pretty desperate at this point for finding any alternative to Maduro, who's become a dictator.
sentences.zh: 这说明国际社会现在已经非常绝望，急于寻找马杜罗的替代者，因为他已经变成了一个独裁者。

sentences.en: So I think when the international countries, when Venezuela's neighbors, when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，当国际社会、当委内瑞拉的邻国、当美国

sentences.en: finally saw that there was someone who was finally willing to take him on face-to-face, they seized the opportunity.
sentences.zh: 终于看到有人愿意与他正面交锋时，他们抓住了这个机会。

sentences.en: And it's a big gamble because they're gambling on someone that doesn't really have a long track record, a long history.
sentences.zh: 这是一场豪赌，因为他们押注在一个并没有长期履历或深厚背景的人身上。

sentences.en: And Venezuela, frankly, is just beginning to know.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，委内瑞拉才刚刚开始了解他。

sentences.en: So countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以像美国这样的国家，

sentences.en: are not so much supporting Guaido as they are supporting the removal and the substitution of Maduro.
sentences.zh: 与其说是在支持瓜伊多，不如说是在支持罢免和替换马杜罗。

sentences.en: If Maduro's gone, someone's got to be in charge.
sentences.zh: 如果马杜罗下台，总得有人掌权。

sentences.en: So if your goal is to get rid of Maduro, your goal also has to be to say who would be the president then.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你的目标是除掉马杜罗，你的目标也必须包括确定谁来担任总统。

sentences.en: And I think that's largely the reason why Guaido has so much backing right now, is because he's not Maduro.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是瓜伊多目前获得如此多支持的主要原因，因为他不是马杜罗。

sentences.en: The United States joins with all freedom-loving nations in recognizing the National Assembly
sentences.zh: 美国与所有热爱自由的国家一道，承认国民议会

sentences.en: as the last vestige of democracy in your country, for it's the only body elected by you, the people.
sentences.zh: 是你们国家民主的最后堡垒，因为它是唯一由你们——人民选举产生的机构。

sentences.en: As such, the United States supports the courageous decision by Juan Guaido, the president of your
sentences.zh: 因此，美国支持你们国民议会主席胡安·瓜伊多

sentences.en: National Assembly, to assert that body's constitutional powers, declare Maduro a usurper, and call for the establishment of a transitional government.
sentences.zh: 所做出的勇敢决定，即主张该机构的宪法权力，宣布马杜罗为篡权者，并呼吁建立过渡政府。

sentences.en: On behalf of the American people, we say to all the good people of Venezuela,
sentences.zh: 我谨代表美国人民，向委内瑞拉所有善良的人民说：

sentences.en: Estamos con ustedes.
sentences.zh: 我们与你们同在。

sentences.en: We are with you.
sentences.zh: 我们与你们同在。

sentences.en: We stand with you.
sentences.zh: 我们支持你们。

sentences.en: And we will stay with you until democracy is restored and you reclaim your birthright of libertad.
sentences.zh: 我们将与你们站在一起，直到民主恢复，直到你们收回属于你们的自由权利。

sentences.en: Muchas gracias.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Y vayan con Dios.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑你们。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，那会怎样？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 这一个月你可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能看到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: So how does Maduro respond to this big international outpouring of support for basically his ouster?
sentences.zh: 那么，马杜罗对国际社会这种几乎是一边倒要求他下台的呼声有何回应？

sentences.en: Well, he threw a big tantrum on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在周三发了一通大脾气。

sentences.en: Starting with declaring that he was cutting diplomatic ties to the U.S., he ordered the personnel of the embassy out in 72 hours.
sentences.zh: 他首先宣布与美国断绝外交关系，并下令大使馆人员在72小时内离境。

sentences.en: This started kind of a fascinating chain of events where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一连串引人入胜的事件，美国

sentences.en: said it wasn't going to leave because it recognized Juan Guaido as the president.
sentences.zh: 表示不会离开，因为它承认胡安·瓜伊多为总统。

sentences.en: And Guaido came out with a statement saying, your embassy officials are welcome to stay.
sentences.zh: 瓜伊多随后发表声明称，欢迎你们的大使馆官员留下来。

sentences.en: We're the government and we would love to have diplomatic relations with you continue just as they had before.
sentences.zh: 我们才是政府，我们非常希望与你们继续保持像以前一样的外交关系。

sentences.en: And how have the people of Venezuela responded to this intervention by countries like the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 那么委内瑞拉人民对美国等国家的这种干预有何反应？

sentences.en: It's been surprising to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It was surprising to me starting maybe 18 months ago when I talked to friends and colleagues who were back in Venezuela and they would ask me what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 大约18个月前，当我与委内瑞拉的朋友和同事交谈，他们问我美国

sentences.en: was going to do about this.
sentences.zh: 打算对此做些什么时，我就感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: And my response would always be, what do you mean what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的回答总是：你们是什么意思，美国

sentences.en: is going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 打算对此做些什么？

sentences.en: You don't certainly want the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你们肯定不希望美国

sentences.en: to be involved in this, do you?
sentences.zh: 卷入其中，对吧？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: has got a kind of a long history in Latin America that people don't like.
sentences.zh: 在拉丁美洲有着一段人们并不喜欢的漫长历史。

sentences.en: I mean, it was the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是美国

sentences.en: that brought Pinochet into power.
sentences.zh: 扶持了皮诺切特上台。

sentences.en: It was the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是美国

sentences.en: that had the coup that got rid of Arbenz Guzman in Guatemala in the 1950s, who was a democratically elected leader.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代策划了政变，推翻了危地马拉民选领导人阿本斯·古斯曼。

sentences.en: U.S.'s history of interventions has been very checkered, but it is a consequence of this strange
sentences.zh: 美国干预的历史非常斑驳，但这正是马杜罗将国家置于这种奇怪

sentences.en: situation that Maduro has put the country in, where an unpopular leader who's presiding over a deep collapse in the country won't go, won't take the exit.
sentences.zh: 境地所带来的后果：一位不受欢迎的领导人，在国家陷入深度崩溃的情况下，既不肯下台，也不肯离开。

sentences.en: The people have actually got to the position, and this isn't everybody in Venezuela, but this is a lot of people in Venezuela who are saying, why doesn't the U.S.
sentences.zh: 人们实际上已经到了这种地步——这并不是说委内瑞拉的所有人，但确实有很多人在问，为什么美国

sentences.en: intervene and try to save us?
sentences.zh: 不介入并试图拯救我们？

sentences.en: And if it's not the U.S., then why don't our own military do this?
sentences.zh: 如果不是美国，那为什么我们自己的军队不这样做？

sentences.en: I think that's what you actually hear much more on the streets of Venezuela, is how could the military stand by and let this man continue to run the country as he does?
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是你在委内瑞拉街头真正听到的声音：军队怎么能袖手旁观，任由这个人继续这样治理国家？

sentences.en: And these two things, asking for intervention and asking for a military coup, are parts of the past that Latin America has been trying to bury for years.
sentences.zh: 而这两件事——要求外部干预和要求军事政变，都是拉丁美洲多年来一直试图埋葬的过去。

sentences.en: So to see them both be part of the landscape again in Venezuela, I find to be a little bit terrifying, frankly.
sentences.zh: 所以看到它们再次成为委内瑞拉的现实，坦白说，我觉得有点可怕。

sentences.en: I met a woman who was protesting in a plaza last year, and she was telling me how much she wanted Donald Trump to intervene.
sentences.zh: 去年我在广场上遇到一位正在抗议的女士，她告诉我她有多希望唐纳德·特朗普能介入。

sentences.en: And this shocked me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: She told me that she'd be happy to see U.S.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，如果能看到美国

sentences.en: tanks circling around Caracas.
sentences.zh: 坦克在加拉加斯周围盘旋，她会很高兴。

sentences.en: And I told her, do you know what this means to have a U.S.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她，你知道美国

sentences.en: invasion of your country?
sentences.zh: 入侵你的国家意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: And this girl was 19.
sentences.zh: 这个女孩才19岁。

sentences.en: I don't think she really knew.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她真的明白。

sentences.en: But you are seeing people that are saying things that you would have thought were preposterous years ago because they've suffered so many years under Maduro.
sentences.zh: 但你确实看到人们在说一些几年前你认为荒谬至极的话，因为他们在马杜罗的统治下受了太多年的苦。

sentences.en: Given the openness because of the situation in Venezuela to countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 鉴于委内瑞拉的局势为美国等国家

sentences.en: weighing in, does the support and the recognition of all these international powers give the opposition more power as they try to take over?
sentences.zh: 介入提供了契机，这种国际力量的支持和承认是否让反对派在试图夺权时拥有了更多权力？

sentences.en: Well, it does and it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，既是也不是。

sentences.en: Symbolically, it's great.
sentences.zh: 从象征意义上讲，这很好。

sentences.en: They have all this support from outside of
sentences.zh: 他们得到了来自委内瑞拉

sentences.en: Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 之外的所有支持。

sentences.en: But what they need is support inside Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 但他们需要的是委内瑞拉内部的支持。

sentences.en: What they have now is all the recognition, but they don't have any of the weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们现在拥有了所有的承认，但他们没有任何武器。

sentences.en: They don't have control over the military.
sentences.zh: 他们没有对军队的控制权。

sentences.en: And ultimately, it's the military that's going to be the arbiter of power in Venezuela and really has been the one that's been holding up Maduro.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，军队才是委内瑞拉权力的仲裁者，也确实是支撑马杜罗的力量。

sentences.en: If anything's going to change, they have to go from holding up Maduro to holding up Guaido.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么要改变，他们必须从支持马杜罗转变为支持瓜伊多。

sentences.en: Ultimately, the power in any constitutional democracy is kind of imaginary.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，任何宪政民主国家的权力在某种程度上都是想象出来的。

sentences.en: It's whether people are willing to respect the norMs. And when they don't, like what's happened
sentences.zh: 这取决于人们是否愿意尊重规则。而当他们不尊重时，就像在委内瑞拉发生的那样，

sentences.en: in Venezuela and the constitution has kind of melted away, it just comes down to the people that have got the weapons as the ones that can say who's in charge.
sentences.zh: 宪法已经名存实亡，最终还是掌握武器的人说了算。

sentences.en: It's the ones with the weapons that are saying Maduro's in charge.
sentences.zh: 正是那些掌握武器的人在说马杜罗说了算。

sentences.en: And if that changes, it's probably going to be the same generals who are the ones that determine that he's not.
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况发生改变，很可能也是同样的将军们决定他不再说了算。

sentences.en: Does that start to look, Nick, like a military coup backed by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 尼克，这看起来像是一场由美国

sentences.en: government?
sentences.zh: 政府支持的军事政变吗？

sentences.en: It does, because you have the U.S.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，因为你有美国

sentences.en: government supporting opposition parties that are supporting military intervention by their own military against the man who's running the government.
sentences.zh: 政府支持反对党，而反对党又支持本国军队对现任政府领导人进行军事干预。

sentences.en: Each of those links is there, and it would link the U.S.
sentences.zh: 每一个环节都环环相扣，这会将美国

sentences.en: to what happens afterward.
sentences.zh: 与之后发生的事情联系起来。

sentences.en: You just don't know.
sentences.zh: 你只是不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: When you ask the armed forces to get involved, it's really up to them what happens next.
sentences.zh: 当你要求武装部队介入时，接下来发生什么真的取决于他们。

sentences.en: So it could all go very badly, and then everybody who supported it would be implicated, including the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以事情可能会变得非常糟糕，那么所有支持它的人都会受到牵连，包括美国。

sentences.en: Yeah, potentially.
sentences.zh: 是的，有可能。

sentences.en: So what exactly is the military weighing right now, knowing that they hold all the power in this equation?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然军队在这个等式中掌握着所有权力，他们现在到底在权衡什么？

sentences.en: So on one side, the military lives very well under Maduro.
sentences.zh: 一方面，军队在马杜罗统治下生活得非常好。

sentences.en: The top brass of the military live lavish lives.
sentences.zh: 军队高层过着奢华的生活。

sentences.en: There's lots of forms of revenue.
sentences.zh: 他们有多种收入来源。

sentences.en: They have lots of control over the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们对经济有很大的控制权。

sentences.en: Many top officers are involved in the drug trade, smuggling, even though there's a big crisis in Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 尽管委内瑞拉正处于严重危机中，但许多高级军官都参与了毒品贸易和走私。

sentences.en: They're not living it at the top.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有处于水深火热之中。

sentences.en: On the other end, they're seeing that this institution, which had been beloved by Venezuelans, is getting increasingly tarnished for being on the side of Maduro.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们看到这个曾经深受委内瑞拉人爱戴的机构，因为站在马杜罗一边而日益蒙羞。

sentences.en: And they're also seeing that so much of the world is now getting behind Guaidó and wondering probably whether Maduro is going to be around forever
sentences.zh: 他们也看到世界上越来越多的人开始支持瓜伊多，可能也在怀疑马杜罗是否会永远存在，

sentences.en: and what they're going to do after Maduro has gone themselves.
sentences.zh: 以及马杜罗下台后他们自己该怎么办。

sentences.en: So this is kind of the dilemma that they're facing.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他们面临的困境。

sentences.en: Whose side do they get on?
sentences.zh: 他们该站在哪一边？

sentences.en: Which side do they think is going to be right in history?
sentences.zh: 他们认为哪一边在历史上会是正确的？

sentences.en: And Nick,
sentences.zh: 尼克，

sentences.en: given how much time you have spent on the ground in Venezuela, I wonder if you have an instinct for which of these will weigh more on the military and how it will go.
sentences.zh: 鉴于你在委内瑞拉实地待了那么久，我想知道你是否有直觉，哪种因素对军队的影响更大，以及事情会如何发展。

sentences.en: Well, I can't say how long it's going to take, but I think that these military officers and rank
sentences.zh: 嗯，我无法说这需要多长时间，但我认为这些军官和普通

sentences.en: and file people are looking out their windows every morning and they're seeing that the crowds are
sentences.zh: 士兵每天早上向窗外看时，都会看到人群

sentences.en: angry and that they're getting bigger and that they need to do something about these crowds and
sentences.zh: 愤怒且规模越来越大，他们需要对这些人群采取行动，

sentences.en: they need to get on the side of them as opposed to the side of the single person who's running the country.
sentences.zh: 他们需要站在人群这一边，而不是站在那个治理国家的单个人这一边。

sentences.en: But I have no idea how they're going to make that decision or when.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道他们将如何做出决定，也不知道何时做出决定。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的消息。

sentences.en: So, Mr. President, later today, day 34 of this partial government shutdown, the Senate will be voting on a proposal to finally end it.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，今天晚些时候，在政府部分停摆的第34天，参议院将投票表决一项旨在最终结束停摆的提案。

sentences.en: On Thursday, for the first time since the partial government shutdown began, the Senate voted on two plans proposed by Republicans and Democrats to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 周四，自政府部分停摆开始以来，参议院首次就共和党和民主党提出的两项重启政府的计划进行了投票。

sentences.en: President's compromise would accomplish three things.
sentences.zh: 总统的妥协方案将实现三件事。

sentences.en: First, it ends the shutdown and resumes pay for federal workers right away.
sentences.zh: 首先，它结束停摆并立即恢复联邦工作人员的工资。

sentences.en: Second, it strikes a bipartisan compromise on the issue of immigration and border security with ideas from both sides.
sentences.zh: 其次，它在移民和边境安全问题上达成了一项两党妥协，采纳了双方的意见。

sentences.en: And third, it provides stable full year funding for the federal government.
sentences.zh: 第三，它为联邦政府提供了稳定的全年资金。

sentences.en: The Republican bill, which would have funded President Trump's proposed border wall, failed by a vote of 50 to 47 and was supported by a single Democrat, Senator Joe
sentences.zh: 共和党的法案本将为特朗普总统提议的边境墙提供资金，但以50票对47票未获通过，仅得到了一位民主党人——西弗吉尼亚州参议员乔·曼钦的支持。

sentences.en: Manchin of West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们的提案允许我们开放政府，然后，在政府开放之后，解决我们在边境安全上的分歧。

sentences.en: Our proposal allows us to open up the government and then, then after government's open, settle our differences over border security.
sentences.zh: 民主党的法案本不会为边境墙提供资金，也以52票对44票未获通过，但得到了六位共和党人的支持，
